candidates.title: Directed codeword repulsion with a control-anchored usage barrier
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the cold run's exported level-0 usage Gini exceeds control, L1-to-L2 branches per code fall below control, train-to-test frequency drift grows, sequence information excess falls below control, or pair-level ER does not rise; any of these is a direct failure of the stated joint requirement.
candidates.risk: The representation displacement may be a poor proxy for behaviour, and the normalized projection can reward a codeword displacement direction that does not preserve useful sequence information. Batch-local soft usage may also be noisy or conflict with naturally nonuniform item frequencies. The frozen evaluation may therefore show improved pair-level separation but worse sequence information, prefix branching, or downstream recall.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The projection term updates the two selected codewords with opposite signed forces along the ordered displacement direction; its positive margin discourages zero separation rather than rewarding pairwise convergence. The usage-floor term pushes source-assigned probability mass away from overused cells and toward underused cells. It does not impose an attractive pairwise codeword-distance term. Hard nearest-code indices are nondifferentiable and are held fixed for the local loss gradient; all differentiable paths remain finite through epsilon and softmax temperature.

candidates.title: Directed soft-assignment transition preservation with a prefix-branch barrier
candidates.falsifier: Reject if exported level-0 Gini rises, prefix branches per code fall, frequency drift grows, sequence information excess falls, or pair-level ER fails to rise. In particular, a healthy soft entropy value with worse exported sequence information falsifies the assumption that this soft transition objective preserves useful hard-code structure.
candidates.risk: The directed distribution-matching term may preserve source assignment statistics rather than improve useful next-item predictability, and the entropy floor can make assignments diffuse. This can preserve occupancy while reducing sequence information or weakening hard SID transitions; the hard export may not reflect the smooth distributions optimized during training.
candidates.codebook_interaction: Gradients pass through the soft source and target assignment probabilities into codebook distances. The objective matches a directed transition distribution to the source distribution and imposes a target-entropy floor; it contains no term that attracts source- and target-selected codeword vectors to one another. The entropy barrier resists a transition distribution supported by a single target code. Softmax temperatures keep gradients finite.

candidates.title: Behaviour-conditioned residual transport with orthogonal codeword-separation protection
candidates.falsifier: Reject if the cold run fails to raise pair-level ER or if any measured requirement fails: exported level-0 Gini above control, fewer L1-to-L2 branches per code, increased train-to-test frequency drift, or lower sequence-information excess. A nonzero measured codebook gradient with unchanged hard assignments and no ER gain also falsifies the proposed route from residual geometry to export change.
candidates.risk: The residual direction and the orthogonal complement may be poorly conditioned when residual displacement is near zero, and a separation hinge can distort codebook geometry without improving ranking. The residual-alignment term may also be satisfied by changes that do not preserve hard assignment sequence information. The floor is batch-local and may not control held-out frequency drift.
candidates.codebook_interaction: The residual-alignment term sends gradients through both assigned codewords via the residuals. The orthogonal-separation hinge acts on the component of the ordered codeword difference perpendicular to the residual displacement, pushing the assigned codewords apart in that component when below delta; it does not reward convergence along the pair axis. The usage-floor penalty pushes probability mass away from overused source cells. Fixed hard indices avoid differentiating through argmin, and eps stabilizes the projection.
